justification: CVE-2024-5908 affected the Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect Android app, where user authentication credentials were written to application log files (PanGPA.log) in a form recoverable by any local actor with access to those logs (CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File). The synthetic vulnerability in Jerboa replicates this exact attack class: the vulnerability.patch removes the sanitizeHeader configuration from Jerboa's Ktor HTTP client Logging plugin. With sanitizeHeader removed and the log level set to ALL, the Authorization header containing the user's JWT Bearer token is written to Android logcat on every authenticated request. An attacker with adb access or READ_LOGS permission can extract the token from logcat and use it to call the Lemmy API on the victim's behalf, reading private messages and other authenticated resources. Both CVE-2024-5908 and this synthetic vulnerability follow the same pattern: an Android app fails to redact sensitive authentication material from its logs, exposing session credentials to local privilege boundaries.
